children.text: Choose exercises that fit the equipment and space you actually have. A bodyweight option removes the need to handle an external load; a dumbbell option adds a load you must select and control. The library includes both. These are different movement setups, not interchangeable prescriptions for every person.

children.text: Use the muscle filter to narrow the library, then open an exercise to read its instructions and equipment list. Difficulty is a broad editorial label, not a readiness test. Start with a movement and range you can control. The language selector changes content between English and Czech; missing translations can fall back to English.
These source-linked starter notes were prepared with AI assistance. They do not assess your individual technique. Stop movements that cause pain and seek qualified guidance when you are unsure.

children.text: A programme contains ordered sessions. Each session contains exercise prescriptions with its own order, set count, repetition range, rest period, and coaching note. Open the linked exercise for movement instructions. A range such as 6–8 describes repetitions within one set; “per side” means each side has its own repetitions. These starter prescriptions are examples, not targets that must be completed.
The sample sessions connect lower-body movements to the Glutes and Calves categories. The anatomy map will use these same content relationships once its 3D asset is integrated.

The sample programmes suggest nonconsecutive practice days. Extend rests, reduce repetitions, or stop a session when needed. Do not treat completing the sample schedule as more important than comfortable, controlled movement.

commonMistakes: Hips sag toward the floor
Elbows flare straight out to the sides
Head drops before the chest

children.text: Start with hands beneath your shoulders and knees supported. Keep your body aligned from knees to head. Bend your elbows to lower your chest under control, then press up. Avoid sagging at your hips. Use a comfortable depth and stop if your wrists hurt.
AI-assisted educational content checked against the source, not an individual assessment or professional coaching review. Stop movements that cause pain.
Source:
https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/13/bent-knee-push-up/

commonMistakes: Boky klesají k podlaze

children.text: Začněte s rukama pod rameny a koleny na podložce. Držte tělo v jedné linii od kolen k hlavě. Pokrčením loktů kontrolovaně spusťte hrudník a vytlačte se zpět. Neprohýbejte boky. Zvolte příjemnou hloubku a při bolesti zápěstí přestaňte.
Vzdělávací obsah s pomocí AI, nikoli osobní posouzení nebo odborná trenérská kontrola. Při bolesti přestaňte.
Source:

children.text: Stand with feet around hip-to-shoulder width. Brace your trunk, bend your hips and knees, and descend within a comfortable range. Keep feet grounded and knees following your toes. Stand smoothly. Shorten the movement if control is lost.

children.text: Lie on your back with bent knees and feet planted. Gently brace, press through your feet, and lift your hips without over-arching your back. Pause comfortably, then lower slowly. Keep the movement controlled rather than chasing maximum height.

children.text: Sit on a stable bench with a backrest and feet grounded. Hold light dumbbells near shoulder level with wrists straight. Press upward without arching your lower back, then lower under control. Use a comfortable range and appropriate assistance when handling the weights.
